gen-gf-grandstander-gf-puritan: Grandstander draws every letter with a pipe-cleaner line that stays wide open and never curls shut. And Puritan takes over below in a plain sans with rounded forms and oversized openings, which gives the loud heading somewhere softer to land.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-sans-anatolian-hie: Audiowide sets its letters like spaced-out tiles, futuristic and tidy. It is best at joining strokes without any thinning, while Noto Sans Anatolian Hieroglyphs is best at staying modern and unfussy, with outward-pointing tips and a lowercase that climbs nearly to cap height.
gen-almendra-display-gf-anek-odia: Almendra Display brings an ornate, literary look, its letters never pinching shut and its lowercase standing pronounced, while Anek Odia stays clean and contemporary beside it. Their strongest shared quality is openness.
gen-eater-gf-roboto: Dark, jagged and a bit menacing. Over many lines, Roboto, a plain sans, keeps its generous round letters and near-level capitals and lowercase quiet enough to read without any strain.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-radio-canada: Chunky, expressive and unashamedly loud. And Radio Canada, a plain sans, lets its tall, full lowercase run on in a steady line with every curve clearly open, so a longer passage moves along smoothly.
gen-gf-funnel-display-gf-ruda: Ruda reads with a sizable x-height and wide-mouthed rounds on a wire-like line. Funnel Display adds spaghetti-like strokes above it, so the sans-serif text and the commanding heading share the same monoline feel.
gen-gf-goldman-gf-saira: Wide, blocky and confident, with round forms like open parentheses. And Saira's see-through s and tall rounded letters make the pair's strongest quality a shared openness, one that never feels cramped.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-sarpanch: Springy, bold and pipe-cleaner thin in every curve. Sarpanch then keeps the sans text compact, with a clearly open lowercase e, so the heading's wide letters have a tighter companion.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-sans-arabic: Noto Sans Arabic opens small letters wide and lifts a pronounced x-height, a plain sans that looks clean and modern. Audiowide's marker-traced, tile-like letters make the pair distinctly futuristic.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-sen: Autour One goes bold and expressive, its round letters entered through clear channels with no hairline shifts. Sen, a modern sans, builds tall lowercase from a constant-weight line, so a longer passage feels smooth and contemporary.
